title: Zn-modified hierarchical ZSM-5 and the role of bimetallic promoters in methanol to aromatic conversion
content: A sustainable one-pot synthesis strategy was developed for the preparation of hierarchical Zn-modified ZSM-5 catalysts using polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as an eco-friendly secondary template, while Ni and Cr were introduced as bimetallic promoters to elucidate their roles in catalytic performance and structure–activity relationships during methanol-to-aromatics (MTA) conversion. Catalytic performance was evaluated in the MTA reaction at 400 °C, atmospheric pressure, and a WHSV of 5 h−1, achieving over 99.5% methanol conversion across all samples. Comprehensive physicochemical characterization demonstrated that PVP-assisted synthesis generated an optimized micro–mesoporous architecture, improved Zn and Al incorporation into the zeolite framework, and enhanced accessibility to active sites. XPS analysis revealed a substantial increase in catalytically active Zn (OH)+ species, particularly in Ni-promoted catalysts, indicating superior Zn dispersion and enhanced dehydrogenation functionality. BET, SEM, and NH3-TPD analyses further confirmed that hierarchical structuring improved diffusion properties, external surface area, and acidity balance, leading to superior catalytic efficiency. Among the prepared catalysts, Zn@PVP/ZC exhibited markedly improved aromatic (67.3%) and BTX (61.8%) selectivity, while ZnNi@PVP/ZC delivered the highest BTX selectivity (67.9%), enhanced catalyst stability, and minimized coke formation due to synergistic Zn–Ni interactions. In contrast, Cr promotion increased excessive strong acidity and accelerated internal coke deposition, resulting in reduced catalytic lifetime and lower BTX productivity. Overall, this work establishes a rational and green catalytic design strategy for high-performance hierarchical ZSM-5 catalysts, highlighting the critical role of bimetallic promotion in optimizing methanol aromatization efficiency.
